a.summary: `tableAccountMetas` is dereferenced without a null check while every sibling overload treats null as "no lookup tables", and the new doc's "With no lookup tables" phrasing invites passing null.
a.failure_scenario: Transaction.createTx(instructions, len, sortedAccounts, (LookupTableAccountMeta[]) null) throws NullPointerException at line 443 instead of building a transaction. A caller who reads the new sentence "With no lookup tables, rebuilds from instructions..." and passes the null they got back from a table resolver gets an NPE, even though createTx(List, int, Map, LookupTableAccountMeta[]) at line 421 and createTx(AccountMeta, List, AddressLookupTable, LookupTableAccountMeta[]) at line 97 both explicitly accept null and route to the no-table path.

b.summary: Only one of the two public array-taking createTx overloads got the new in-place-mutation javadoc; the AddressLookupTable overload compacts the caller's array identically and is still undocumented — and it is the code path the documented overload's own one-table promise is delegated to.
b.failure_scenario: A consumer holds its own sorted AccountMeta[] and calls Transaction.createTx(instructions, serializedInstructionLength, sorted, lookupTable) (the AddressLookupTable overload at line 266). Lines 273-320 permute `sorted` in place exactly as the documented overload does — message accounts to the front, lookup accounts to the tail. The caller then reuses `sorted` (for a second transaction, or to map account index -> meta) and gets the permuted array: with input [payer, lookupA, lookupB, program] the array is [payer, program, lookupA, lookupB] on return, so index-based lookups and any second createTx call read the wrong accounts. Nothing at the declaration warns them. The same consumer reading the newly documented 4-arg overload is told 'With one or more lookup tables, compacts sortedAccounts in place' — but the one-table case is delivered by line 447 delegating to this undocumented sibling, so the documented sentence is realized by a method whose own signature carries no such notice.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
